battle.name: 唐滅大齊之戰
battle.theater: 中原汴河兩岸與曹州泰山一線
battle.brief: 884年春，河東節度使李克用率五萬兵自河中南渡，連破大齊軍於太康、汴河、王滿渡；宣武節度使朱全忠在王滿渡擊潰黃巢主力，齊軍北走封丘，終於七月覆滅於泰山狼虎谷。卡面所繪的希臘重步兵方陣並未出現在中唐戰場，但本卡取其「結陣正面」之理對照唐軍步兵的密集隊形，記錄唐滅大齊的收官一戰。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 唐與大齊兩方。唐朝一方以流亡京師的僖宗朝廷為名，實權分散在節度使與宦官手中：河東節度使李克用領沙陀部落的河東、雁門、忻代諸州兵，是討齊的主力；宣武節度使朱全忠握汴州，控制中原的運河與糧道；關中則有僖宗行在鳳翔，隨軍護從以神策軍與各道鎮兵組成。大齊一方是黃巢建國後收攏的起義殘部與新附的唐軍降將，核心為尚讓、趙璋、孟楷等原黃巢部將，兵源以鹽販、失業農戶、逃卒為主，並收編各州縣的團練與投降官軍，駐防重心由長安逐步退向陳州、曹州一帶。這場戰爭其實是唐朝藩鎮武力與起義殘軍的收官之戰：朝廷在兵源、馬匹與財政上都依賴地方節度使，因此即便收復兩京，權力也並未回歸中央。
countriesEn: There were two sides, the Tang and the Great Qi. On the Tang side the name was kept alive by Emperor Xizong's court in exile, while real authority was split between the regional jiedushi and the eunuchs: Li Keyong, jiedushi of Hedong, led the Shatuo people together with the troops of Hedong, Yanmen, Xinzhou and Daizhou, and became the main force of the campaign against Qi; Zhu Quanzhong, jiedushi of Xuanwu, held Bianzhou and therefore the canal and the grain route of the central plain; in Guanzhong the emperor's camp sat at Fengxiang with an escort made up of the Divine Strategy Guard and the garrisons of the various circuits. The Qi side was the surviving core of the rebellion together with newly submitted Tang officers, led by former lieutenants of Huang Chao such as Shang Rang, Zhao Zhang and Meng Kai; its soldiers came mainly from salt smugglers, jobless peasants and deserters, and it absorbed the local militia and surrendered government troops of many prefectures, its defensive centre gradually shifting from Chang'an back towards Chenzhou and Caozhou. This war was in fact the closing round between the military power of the Tang's regional governors and the remnants of the rebellion. In troops, horses and money the court depended on the provincial commanders, so even after the two capitals were recovered, power did not return to the centre.
people: 唐僖宗李儇自880年出奔成都、883年再幸鳳翔，全程由太監田令孜挾持，是這場戰爭裡最被動的一位君主；真正決定戰局的是李克用。他是沙陀人，父親李赤心被朝廷賜名朱邪，他原以李朱邪之名效力，883年受詔為河東節度使、復李姓，率沙陀騎兵自河東南下，成為唐軍真正的統帥。朱全忠原名朱溫，本為黃巢部將，882年在同州歸唐，朝廷賜名全忠，此後以宣武節度使的身分在汴河一線追擊黃巢，並逐步吸納齊軍降將。齊王黃巢是曹州冤句人，出身鹽商，進士不第之後組織武裝押運走私，875年與子黃揆、姪黃恩鄴等八人起兵，881年即帝位於含元殿。他用人極寬，尚讓居太尉兼中書令，趙璋任侍中，孟楷、蓋洪為左右僕射，皮日休為翰林學士——這份名單說明起義軍已吸納唐代官僚制度的外殼。883年尚讓率十餘萬圍華州，刺史杜彥光糧盡力戰幾乎不保；884年尚讓降唐，與時溥部將李師悅同追黃巢，戰至泰山狼虎谷，黃巢為部下林言所殺，其子黃邶亦死於鄆州項城一役。
peopleEn: Emperor Xizong, who fled to Chengdu in 880 and again to Fengxiang in 883 and was kept in the grip of the eunuch Tian Lingzi throughout, was the most passive sovereign in this war; the man who decided the outcome was Li Keyong. A Shatuo, Li Keyong's father Li Chixin had been granted the name Zhu Ye by the court, and he himself first served under the name Li Zhu Ye; in 883 he was appointed jiedushi of Hedong and restored to the surname Li, and he marched south from Hedong at the head of the Shatuo cavalry, becoming the real commander of the Tang armies. Zhu Quanzhong, originally named Zhu Wen, had been one of Huang Chao's generals and came over to the Tang in 882 at Tongzhou, where the court granted him the name Quanzhong; as jiedushi of Xuanwu he then pursued Huang Chao along the Bian River and steadily absorbed the defectors from the Qi army. Huang Chao himself was a native of Yuanjul in Caozhou, born into a salt merchant family; after failing the imperial examination he organised armed escort convoys for smuggling, and in 875 he rose with his son Huang Kui, his nephew Huang Enyun and six others, taking the imperial throne in the Hall of Contained Origin in 881. He was generous in appointments, putting Shang Rang in the joint posts of Grand Commandant and Imperial Counselor, Zhao Zhang as Minister of the Household, Meng Kai and Gai Hong as Left and Right Vice Presidents, and Pi Rixiu as a Hanlin academician; that list shows the rebels had taken over the outer shell of Tang bureaucracy. In 883 Shang Rang led more than a hundred thousand men to besiege Huazhou, where the prefect Du Yanguang held out with food nearly exhausted; in 884 Shang Rang surrendered to the Tang and joined Li Shiyue, sent out by the jiedushi of Wuning Shi Pu, in the pursuit that ran all the way to Langhu Valley in the Mount Tai range, where Huang Chao was killed by his own subordinate Lin Yan, while his son Huang Bi fell in the fighting at Xiangcheng in Yunzhou.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是希臘重步兵，約公元前五百年，配圓盾、方盾、長矛、青銅頭盔與脛甲，作戰依靠方陣。公元前五百年希臘重步兵在中國，並非此戰的裝備；本卡採用的是「以結陣正面取勝」這條對照線，用以說明中唐步兵如何以密集隊形承擔戰鬥。884年唐軍與齊軍真正用得上的，是弩與弓箭——唐軍倚重固定弩、臂弩與床弩，齊軍則以弓箭、標槍配合大量近身兵刃；步兵普遍用長矛與唐刀，裝甲輕而數量多。騎兵是決定性兵種，沙陀騎兵多不著重甲，攜帶馬槊、長弓與短刀，依靠騎射與突擊作戰；齊軍騎兵同樣以流動射擊擾亂唐軍側翼。攻城方面，唐軍備有撞車、雲梯與攻城塔，齊軍在陳州城下掘塹五重、以數百支大槌攻破城垣，圍城近三百日；糧秣主要靠運河與汴河的水運，黃巢北走後因糧盡不能追，這一點直接決定了李克用放棄追擊。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Greek hoplite, around 500 BC, equipped with round and figure-of-eight shields, a long spear, a bronze helmet and greaves, and fighting in the phalanx. Greek hoplites in China five hundred years before the common era were not equipment in this war; what the card borrows is the parallel line of 'winning with the frontage of a formed body', used here to explain how mid-Tang infantry carried the fighting through their dense formations. What the Tang and the Qi actually fought with in 884 was the crossbow and the bow: the Tang relied on fixed crossbows, hand crossbows and mounted tube crossbows, while the Qi matched bows and javelins with a great many close-combat weapons; infantry generally carried long spears and Tang sabres, and were lightly armoured but numerous. Cavalry was the decisive arm. Shatuo horsemen were mostly unarmoured, carrying the long cavalry lance, the long bow and a short sword, and fought by shooting from the saddle and by sudden charge; the Qi cavalry likewise used fluid mounted shooting to disorder the flanks of the Tang line. For siege work the Tang brought rams, scaling ladders and siege towers, while the Qi at Chenzhou dug fivefold trenches and worked the wall with several hundred heavy mauls, keeping the city invested for close to three hundred days. Supply came chiefly by water on the canals and the Bian River, and once Huang Chao turned north the pursuers were checked by want of grain, which was exactly what caused Li Keyong to give up the chase.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術主軸是唐軍「騎兵為主、步兵結陣」的組合。沙陀騎兵不與齊軍糾纏，而是以「合而離、離而合」的游騎方式反覆掠襲其側翼與糧道：自河中南渡後，李克用連敗齊軍於太康、汴河、王滿渡；883年華州之圍，華州刺史杜彥光力守數月、糧盡欲潰，援軍及時而至，尚讓解圍而去。884年春汴河一線，朱全忠的宣武軍與李克用的沙陀軍在王滿渡形成南北夾擊，齊軍主力當場崩潰，部將李讜、葛從周、楊能、霍存、張歸霸等紛紛降朱，齊軍向北急走，在封丘遇大雨，黃巢收拾散兵不足千人奔兗州，李克用軍晝夜追馳，終因糧盡而返。決戰階段，唐軍以追擊部隊與武寧節度使時溥所遣李師悅的萬人為先鋒，降將尚讓為向導，在泰山狼虎谷四面合圍，完成最後一擊。對照希臘方陣的原理可見：雙方勝負不取決於個人武藝，而取決於能否把散兵收成可傳遞體力的集體。
tacticsEn: The tactical axis of this war was the Tang combination of cavalry in front and infantry formed up behind. The Shatuo horsemen did not get entangled with the Qi columns; they worked in the old steppe fashion of 'joining and then dispersing, dispersing and then joining', raiding the flanks and the supply lines again and again. After crossing the river south from Hezhong, Li Keyong beat the Qi in succession at Taikang, on the Bian River and at Wangman Crossing. In the siege of Huazhou in 883 the prefect Du Yanguang held for several months until his food was nearly gone and the city was about to open, and the relieving force arrived in time so that Shang Rang withdrew. On the Bian River in the spring of 884 the Xuanwu army of Zhu Quanzhong and the Shatuo army of Li Keyong closed on Wangman Crossing from north and south; the main body of the Qi broke on the spot, and generals such as Li Tan, Ge Congzhou, Yang Neng, Huo Cun and Zhang Guiba came over to Zhu one after another. The Qi army hurried north, was caught by heavy rain at Fengqiu, and Huang Chao gathered fewer than a thousand men and ran for Yanzhou, while Li Keyong's troops rode through day and night in the pursuit and finally turned back for want of grain. In the decisive stage the Tang used the pursuing columns and the ten thousand men of Li Shiyue, sent by the jiedushi of Wuning Shi Pu, as the spearhead, with the surrendered Shang Rang as guide, and closed in on Langhu Valley in the Mount Tai range from all sides for the last blow. Set against the principle of the Greek phalanx, the lesson is clear: on neither side did the outcome turn on individual valour, but on whether scattered men could be gathered into a body whose strength passes from man to man.
data: 時間線：875年，黃巢起兵；880年十二月，黃巢軍入長安；881年正月十六，黃巢即帝位於含元殿，國號大齊，年號金統；882年九月，朱溫在同州降唐，賜名全忠；883年，李克用為河東節度使，率師南下；884年春，李克用率兵五萬自河中南渡，連敗齊軍於太康、汴河、王滿渡；884年三月，朱全忠於王滿渡大敗黃巢；884年六月十五日，時溥遣李師悅率兵萬人，與降將尚讓合追；884年六月十七日，黃巢在泰山狼虎谷為部下林言所殺，其子黃邶在鄆州項城被追殺。距離與行程：河中蒲州至王滿渡一線約四百華里，封丘至泰山狼虎谷約六百華里，黃巢自長安北撤至曹州、兗州一線達千餘里。數字方面有據可查者為李克用五萬人、李師悅一萬人、封丘集散兵不足千人；華州之圍約歷數月，陳州被圍近三百日。齊軍兵力在史籍中常寫作數十萬乃至百萬，與其鹽販出身、兩年內由數千膨脹至數十萬的記載相比，顯係誇大，宜作量級看待。傷亡數字無可信記載，本條不作推算。
dataEn: The timeline: 875, Huang Chao rises; December 880, the Huang Chao army enters Chang'an; the sixteenth day of the first month of 881, Huang Chao takes the imperial seat in the Hall of Contained Origin and proclaims Great Qi with the era name Jintong; September 882, Zhu Wen comes over to the Tang at Tongzhou and is granted the name Quanzhong; 883, Li Keyong is made jiedushi of Hedong and marches south; in the spring of 884 Li Keyong takes fifty thousand men across the river from Hezhong and defeats the Qi in succession at Taikang, on the Bian River and at Wangman Crossing; in the third month of 884 Zhu Quanzhong routs Huang Chao at Wangman Crossing; on the fifteenth day of the sixth month of 884 Shi Pu sends Li Shiyue with ten thousand men, joining the surrendered Shang Rang in the pursuit; on the seventeenth day of the sixth month of 884 Huang Chao is killed by his subordinate Lin Yan at Langhu Valley in the Mount Tai range, and his son Huang Bi is hunted down at Xiangcheng in Yunzhou. Distances and stages: roughly four hundred li from Puzhou in Hezhong to the line of Wangman Crossing, about six hundred li from Fengqiu to Langhu Valley, and more than a thousand li from Chang'an north to Caozhou and Yanzhou. The figures that can be relied on are the fifty thousand of Li Keyong, the ten thousand of Li Shiyue, and the fewer than a thousand stragglers gathered at Fengqiu; the siege of Huazhou lasted several months and Chenzhou was invested for close to three hundred days. The strength of the Qi is often written in the histories as several hundred thousand or even a million, which against a rebel force that began as a few thousand salt smugglers and swelled within two years is plainly an exaggeration and should be read as an order of magnitude. No trustworthy casualty figures survive, and none are estimated here.
cause: 起事的原因有遠近兩層。遠因是唐末的結構性崩壞：懿宗以來兩浙、劍南、嶺南戰事不息，軍費無著，朝廷把漕運與鹽利擠壓到極限，乾符元年的水旱災荒又令河東、河南一帶的糧價騰貴，饑民被迫賣兒鬻女；朝廷於是募兵，結果節度使掌兵、糧源與稅收，中央對邊鎮失控，黃巢一伙鹽販正是在這樣的縫隙裡以武裝押運的形式聚起數千人的核心。881年黃巢建大齊後發出的檄文，把矛頭指向宦官，指斥「宦豎柄朝，垢蠹紀綱」；他佔據兩京卻不建立經濟政策，也不肅清關中各鎮的兵，而是縱兵搜括、濫殺，軍紀很快失控，失去民心，這使唐廷的每一次反攻都得到地方響應。直接導火線則是883年僖宗在鳳翔下詔，任李克用為河東節度使、令其率沙陀軍討齊；此時黃巢已放棄關中、主力北撤，雙方在汴河與曹州一線必然相遇，唐滅大齊的最後一戰由此鋪開。
causeEn: The outbreak has both a remote and a proximate layer. The remote cause is the structural breakdown of the late Tang: since the reign of Emperor Yizong there had been no end of fighting in Liangzhe, Jiannan and Lingnan, the war effort went unpaid, and the court squeezed the canal revenues and the salt monopoly to the limit; the floods and droughts of the first year of the Qianfu era sent grain prices soaring in Hedong and the central plain, and hungry families sold their children to survive. The court then recruited soldiers, and as a result the regional governors held the troops, the grain and the taxes, and the centre lost control of the frontier. It was into exactly such a gap that a gang of salt smugglers led by Huang Chao grew a core of several thousand men under armed escort. When Huang Chao founded Great Qi in 881 his proclamation pointed at the eunuchs, accusing them of holding court power and defiling the discipline of the state. Holding the two capitals yet building no economic policy, failing to disarm the garrisons in Guanzhong, and letting his troops rob and kill at will, he lost military discipline and popular support in short order, which meant that every counter-offensive by the Tang found local response. The proximate trigger was the decree of 883, issued at Fengxiang, appointing Li Keyong jiedushi of Hedong and ordering his Shatuo army against Qi. By then Huang Chao had already given up Guanzhong and moved his main body north, so the two sides were bound to meet along the Bian River and around Caozhou, and the last battle to destroy Great Qi unfolded from there.
impact: 大齊政權前後不足四年，終結於泰山狼虎谷，兩京回到唐室，朝廷改元光啟。但唐並未因此復興：真正的收兵方是河東李克用與汴州朱全忠，兩人各自擁兵自重，中央禁軍在亂軍與黨爭中耗盡，節度使的軍、財、官三權合一，藩鎮割據的格局由此定型。李克用因戰功進封晉王，河東沙陀武裝從此深入中原；朱全忠則在收拾黃巢殘部中盡收其精騎，收編李讜、葛從周、張歸霸等部將，把宣武軍擴成中原最大的武裝集團。戰後唐廷追究太監田令孜之責，其人先被幽禁、後被外貶，宦官勢力一度受挫，但禁軍的問題並未解決。經濟上，汴河沿線與關中的州縣飽受兵禍，倉廩府庫被焚掠一空，兩京的市井難以復舊，租庸調的徵發基礎更加脆弱；北方邊鎮的軍糧依賴江淮轉運，漕運線上的爭奪從此更加激烈。可以確定的是，黃巢之亂雖平，亂的真正受益者是藩鎮，而這正是唐末五代亂局的源頭。
impactEn: The Great Qi regime lasted less than four years and ended in Langhu Valley in the Mount Tai range; the two capitals returned to the Tang and the court changed the era to Guangqi. But the Tang did not revive. The real beneficiaries of the fighting were Li Keyong of Hedong and Zhu Quanzhong of Bianzhou, each of whom now held troops of his own; the central palace guard had been used up in the chaos and in the factional struggles, and the jiedushi now combined military, fiscal and administrative power in one pair of hands, so the pattern of territorial fragmentation was fixed from that moment on. Li Keyong was raised to Prince of Jin for his part in the war, and the Shatuo military establishment of Hedong entered the central plain for good. Zhu Quanzhong, clearing up the remnants of Huang Chao, took over the best of the rebel horse, absorbed generals such as Li Tan, Ge Congzhou and Zhang Guiba, and built the Xuanwu army into the largest armed force in the central plain. After the victory the court fixed responsibility on the eunuch Tian Lingzi, who was first confined and later banished, so the eunuch faction was checked for a time, but the problem of the guard was not solved. Economically the prefectures along the Bian River and in Guanzhong had been worn out by the war, the granaries and treasuries were burnt and looted, the markets of the two capitals could not be restored, and the basis for collecting the land tax and the labour service grew more fragile; the grain for the northern commands still had to come down from Jianghuai, and the struggle over the canal route became fiercer from then on. What can be said with certainty is this: the rebellion of Huang Chao was put down, but the ones who profited from it were the regional governors, and that is the origin of the disorder of the late Tang and the Five Dynasties.
result: 884年七月，黃巢死於泰山狼虎谷，大齊軍主力瓦解：其子黃邶在鄆州項城被追殺，部將或降或散，尚讓降唐並引導追兵，葛從周、楊能、霍存、張歸霸等相繼歸於朱全忠。陳州一線的圍城工具與各州縣的團練、自守武裝隨大齊崩潰而陸續散去，關中的軍鎮由唐廷重新編制，僖宗自鳳翔還京，兩京復歸，收復後的長安與洛陽只剩空殼般的宮室與荒蕪的坊市。對這場戰爭的總結是：起義軍在戰術上並不弱——尚讓能以十餘萬眾長期圍困華州、孟楷能以先鋒深入河南——敗在缺乏可持續的財政與地方治理，加上唐廷在最後三年得以集中河東、宣武兩支可靠的武裝。就兵器而言，此役也留下了一個可供比較的樣本：唐軍最後靠沙陀騎兵的機動與突擊取勝，而非靠密集步兵方陣的正面硬碰；同一時期在歐亞西端，以結陣正面為核心的重步兵傳統已隨羅馬帝國解體而不再作為常備軍制存在，卡面這件希臘重步兵的方陣，留在本戰役的記錄裡，只能作為一條技術對照線，而不是戰場所用的裝備。
resultEn: In the seventh month of 884 Huang Chao was killed at Langhu Valley in the Mount Tai range and the main body of the Great Qi army dissolved: his son Huang Bi was hunted down at Xiangcheng in Yunzhou, his generals either surrendered or scattered, Shang Rang came over to the Tang and guided the pursuers, and Ge Congzhou, Yang Neng, Huo Cun and Zhang Guiba passed one by one to Zhu Quanzhong. The siege works in the line of Chenzhou and the local militia and self-defence bands of the prefectures fell away with the collapse of Qi, the commands in Guanzhong were reorganised by the court, and Xizong returned from Fengxiang to the capital, so that the two capitals were recovered, though the Chang'an and Luoyang that came back were little more than empty shells of palaces and desolate ward districts. The sum of the war is this: the rebels were not tactically weak, since Shang Rang could besiege Huazhou for months with more than a hundred thousand men and Meng Kai could drive deep into Henan as the spearhead; they were defeated by the lack of sustainable finance and of local government, and by the fact that in the last three years the Tang court was able to concentrate two dependable armed bodies, those of Hedong and Xuanwu. As for weapons, the campaign left a usable comparison: the Tang finally won through the mobility and sudden charge of the Shatuo cavalry rather than through a frontal collision of massed infantry in the phalanx. At the same moment, in the far west of Eurasia, the tradition of heavy infantry built around the frontage of a formed body had already gone with the dissolution of the Roman empire and no longer existed as a standing military system; the phalanx of the Greek hoplite on the card survives in the record of this battle only as a technical line of comparison, not as equipment that fought on the field.
